    Thin ray categories #

    A thin ray category has at most one nonzero morphism between two objects. It is given by a relation le x y ("there is a nonzero morphism x → y") and a predicate nz x y z ("the composite x → y → z is nonzero"), subject to the axioms of RayCat.ThinData. All cleaving diagrams of BO13a §2.2 (trees with zero relations, commutative squares, diamonds) are of this kind.

    source
    structure LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.ThinData (V : Type) :
    Type

    The data of a thin ray category on a finite type of objects.

    • le : V → V → Prop
    • nz : V → V → V → Prop
    • refl (x : V) : self.le x x
    • antisymm (x y : V) : self.le x y → self.le y x → x = y
    • nz_le (x y z : V) : self.le x y → self.le y z → self.nz x y z → self.le x z
    • nz_left (x z : V) : self.le x z → self.nz x x z
    • nz_right (x z : V) : self.le x z → self.nz x z z
    • assoc (x y z w : V) : self.le x y → self.le y z → self.le z w → (self.nz x y z ∧ self.nz x z w ↔ self.nz y z w ∧ self.nz x y w)

      Associativity: a triple composite is nonzero computed either way.
